task.question: How many years after retiring following the 2022 Beijing Games did Alysa Liu launch her comeback, per ESPN?
task.evidence: Liu retired after the 2022 Beijing Games only to launch a triumphant comeback two years later.
task.page: Olympic champ Alysa Liu withdraws from figure skating worlds

answer:
Alysa Liu announced that she plans to return in the 2027-28 skating season, which means she will be launching her comeback five years after retiring following the 2022 Beijing Games. 

FINAL: 5 years

[Journeyman goalie Matt Tomkins stars for hometown Oilers in seventh NHL start] NEW YORK -- Matt Tomkins ' hockey journey started in the Edmonton suburb of Sherwood Park. Along the way, he tended goal at Ohio State, played for teams like the Indy Fuel and Rockford IceHogs in the minors and Frolunda and Farjestads BK in Sweden and became Canada's starter at the 2022 Olympics in the Beijing bubble when the NHL pulled out at the last minute. "It's been a long road, for sure," Tomkins said. "It's taken me a lot of different places." He finally debuted in the top league in the world in 2023, a few months after turning 29. Now 32, he is back with his hometown Oilers and on Sunday was spectacular in backstopping them to an 11th win in 15 games to start the season. Making his first start since April 17, 2024, and seventh in the NHL, Tomkins was the first star of the game for stopping 27 of the 28 shots he faced and beating the New York Rangers 4-1 at Madison Square Garden. "He was awesome for us," said captain Connor McDavid . "He just gave us a chance to win. ... He was just solid, honestly: made the saves he needed to and gave us a chance." Tomkins wasn't sure he'd get this chance again, let alone for the team he grew up cheering for. During the 928 days since he started for the Tampa Bay Lightning in their 2023-24 regular-season finale, he had played in 74 games in the American Hockey League for the Syracuse Crunch and Bakersfield Condors. "The human element, there's maybe a little bit of doubt," Tomkins said. "Not from your ability, but more so just the opportunity. There's only 64 jobs at any given time and incredible goalies all over the world are fighting for them every single day." It took injuries to fellow goalies Devon Levi and Frederik Andersen , plus the scheduling of games on back-to-back days this weekend, to get Tomkins this opportunity. Taking advantage of it brought joy to not only him but his teammates out of appreciation for what it has taken for him to reach this point. "So nice," McDavid said. "He's a great dude, an unbelievable dude. He worked so hard this summer in Edmonton and just so happy for him. Obviously, it's a cool place -- a cool place to play, a special building. Really cool. I'm happy for him." With Tristan Jarry coming off back-to-back shutouts and Levi and Andersen working their way back to being available, this may be Tomkins' only chance in his latest call-up. With the spotlight shining on him, he took full advantage. "It's been a couple of years since I've played in the league, so definitely excited to get the nod," Tomkins said. [Alysa Liu skipping '26-27 skating season to 'recalibrate'] Olympic gold medalist Alysa Liu announced she's taking the upcoming figure skating season off and plans to return in 2027-28. In a social media post Tuesday, Liu wrote that she's looking to "take the time to recalibrate." "I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve," she wrote, in part, on Instagram. "It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth. I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot. So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far. See yall soon!!" Liu, 21, became the first American woman to win a Winter Games gold medal in more than two decades back in February in Milan and returned to the United States a national hero. She previously withdrew from this year's figure skating world championships a month after the Winter Games ended, a common occurrence for Olympic athletes. In an interview with NBC Sports , Liu said she'll spend the time off continuing to train and hone her skills. "I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve, and then I'll be back after that is done," she said in the interview. "But I'll still be cheering on all my competitors and my teammates, and I'm really excited." Liu had been scheduled to compete in the first leg of Skate America's Grand Prix in Everett, Washington on Nov. 13-15 before her announcement Tuesday.
